chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The origin of the pigeons of the Sanctuary is the remnant of the pigeons that belonged to Ismail ibn Ibrahim (peace be upon him) — he kept them as he was comforted by them.
Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: It is recommended that you keep a bird with clipped wings to be comforted by it, for fear of the vermin.

key_terms.الْهَوَامّ: Harmful crawling creatures, vermin, insects — things that bite or sting; keeping birds was believed to deter them
key_terms.حَمَامُ الْحَرَمِ: The pigeons of the Sanctuary (al-Masjid al-Haram in Mecca), which have special protected status in Islamic law
key_terms.مَقْصُوص: Clipped, with wings trimmed so the bird cannot fly away — a method of keeping domesticated birds
key_terms.يُسْتَحَبُّ: It is recommended (mustahabb) — a jurisprudential category meaning a meritorious act that earns reward but whose omission is not sinful

ai.seo_question: Why are the pigeons of Mecca's al-Haram considered sacred in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) traces the origin of the sacred pigeons of al-Haram back to Prophet Ismail (AS), son of Ibrahim (AS), who kept them for companionship and comfort. The Imam then issues a jurisprudential recommendation (istihbab) that one should keep a clipped-wing bird for comfort, as a practical measure against harmful vermin. This hadith connects the sacred geography of Mecca with Prophetic practice and provides a legal ruling encouraging the keeping of domesticated birds, rooted in the example set by the prophets Ibrahim and Ismail at the foundation of the Haram.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The original pigeon of the Sanctuary of the rest of the pigeons was for Ismail<sup>as</sup> Bin Ibrahim<sup>as</sup>. He<sup>as</sup> took it as he<sup>as</sup> was comfortable with it’.
So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is recommended for you to take a clipped bird to be comfortable with it, if fear of the vermin’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtariy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The real free pigeon remaining is the pigeon that belonged to Tsma‘il ibn Ibrahim, ‘Alayhima al-Salam, who kept it for comfort.
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It is preferable to keep a bird with clipped wings for comfort and for (to dispel) fear from vermin.’”
